title: Briefing for 2026-10-28
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-10-28: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: World Bank's Banga: Availability of capital 'not really an issue' as AI demand drives up borrowing costs. Fed rate hikes are coming, but not this week: CNBC survey. Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey. UK inflation jumps to 3.5% — cementing rate hike expectations. Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes. Retail traders buy the dip on chip stocks — but Robinhood gets burned by the crypto market.
global: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin. Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case. Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison in sex trafficking case. Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase. Donald Trump's biggest economic problem looks strangely familiar. Landline switchover could cut people off in emergency, minister warned.
philippines: SC: Employees cannot be forced to retire before age 65 without consent. [Vantage Point] One peso, two fortunes: The hidden energy bill. Saudi’s biggest oil refinery hit with missile, say Yemen’s Houthis. Hegseth likely to face questions on US role in Indo-Pacific at ASEAN summit.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
